key_insight: Constraining task updates to a shared low‑rank LoRA subspace lets a single, tiny adapter continually learn new tasks with almost no forgetting and without replay or storing multiple adapters.
problem_solved: Enables strict (or near‑strict) continual learning for large pretrained models while avoiding catastrophic forgetting, replay buffers, and the storage/compute overhead of many separate adapters.
method: Introduce Share: a single parameter‑efficient LoRA adapter whose update space is a shared low‑rank subspace across tasks.
For each new task, project updates into the shared subspace (and optionally a small task‑specific component), using orthogonalization/regularization to preserve earlier task directions.
Train only the low‑rank factors (kept small) so adaptation is cheap in compute and memory, and knowledge integrates into the shared subspace instead of isolated adapters.
impact: Practitioners can continually adapt large models on-device or in constrained infra with minimal memory and compute, achieving near zero‑forgetting without data replay or proliferating adapters — simplifying deployment and maintenance.
visual_elements: Diagram: pretrained model + single LoRA adapter with arrows showing multiple tasks projecting into a shared low‑rank subspace
Chart: forgetting curves comparing Share vs standard LoRA and replay methods (Share showing near‑flat loss/accuracy across tasks)
Schematic: training pipeline per task (task data → project into shared subspace → update low‑rank factors) highlighting no replay and small memory footprint
Bar chart/table: memory & compute cost vs accuracy for Share, multi‑adapter LoRA, and full fine‑tuning
paper_title: Shared LoRA Subspaces for almost Strict Continual Learning
paper_authors: Prakhar Kaushik, Ankit Vaidya, Shravan Chaudhari, Rama Chellappa, Alan Yuille
